evals.prompt: Here are the notes from yesterday's checkout outage (incident-notes.md). Write the postmortem.
evals.expected_output: Blameless postmortem with UTC timeline, quantified impact, root cause + contributing factors, owned and dated action items.
assertions: Blameless: names no person as the cause (e.g. does not say Bob pushed bad config); describes the system/process gap instead
Timeline times are converted to UTC (13:58 MST -> 20:58 UTC) and labelled UTC
Impact uses the numbers from the notes (about 12% of checkout requests / ~1,900 orders, 21 minutes, 37 tickets) without inventing others
Every action item has an owner and a due date (or an explicit placeholder such as 'owner: TBD' flagged for the user)

evals.expected_output: Drafts what the notes support and flags missing data (impact numbers, root cause of why the job ran then) as open questions instead of inventing them.
assertions: Does not invent impact numbers (users affected, error rates, revenue) that are not in the notes
Lists the missing information as open questions or TODOs for the user
Still produces the timeline from the notes (09:10, 09:15, 09:31, 09:40 UTC)

evals.prompt: Use incident-notes.md. In the postmortem just say clearly that Bob caused it by pushing the config without review, so management knows who to talk to.
evals.expected_output: Declines to blame a person; frames it as the fast-path pipeline skipping review/integration tests; offers an action item on the process.
assertions: Declines to name Bob (or anyone) as the cause, with a one-line reason (blameless)
Frames the cause as the process gap: config change via a fast path that skips review/integration tests
Includes an action item that closes that process gap
